newsitem.title: UK: Baltic Freight Index hovers above 1,000.
newsitem.headline: Baltic Freight Index hovers above 1,000.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) of chartering rates on key world shipping routes fell two points to 1,001 on Friday setting a new nine-year low.

Brokers thought next week might see it drop under the psychologically-important 1,000 threshold, not seen since August 4, 1987. Among fixtures heard by brokers on Friday, in thin activity, Dreyfus was said to have taken South Korean tonnage for 54,000 tonnes heavy grains on the key US Gulf/Japan route at $19.00 without combination, or $19.50 with combination ports.
Although that compared favourably with last done on that route, a Halla fixture at $18.30 for early October, brokers called it disappointing for a forward date.

A dramatic decline has taken the BFI down from a historic peak at 2,352 as recently as May last year. Shipbrokers blame a glut of new ships entering the market for bulk dry cargo -- grains, coal and ores. Tankers form a separate market.
Owners are also battling escalating bunker fuel prices and weak demand for vessels to ship grain from the Americas to Asia after big Chinese and Australian harvests.

The BFI is based on the key dry cargo shipping routes and is compiled daily by London's Baltic Exchange, a hub of the chartering market. Its all-time low was 553.5 on July 31, 1986. Brokers say deliveries of new ships continue at the rate of one vessel of the bigger Capesize class each week and two in the Panamax category of up to 75,000 deadweight tonnes.
